- Overestimate prices after strong sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.6) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate when sentiment is consistently low or negative (sentiment < 0.3) — model misses downward pressure or mean reversion.
- Lag in response to recent sentiment shifts — model often reacts 1–2 days too late, especially after sentiment turns sharply.
- Overweight recent price momentum in forecasts — model ignores mean reversion when prices are trending sharply.
- When sentiment is high and prices are rising, model tends to overpredict peak — correct by reducing forecast slope after 3–5 consecutive days of upward momentum.
- When sentiment is low and prices are falling, model often underpredicts the drop — adjust downward by 5–10% of recent range if sentiment < 0.2.
- Avoid extrapolating from 30-day history — model overfits to recent trends; use sentiment to dampen forecast if sentiment is volatile or inconsistent.
